newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian All Ordinaries hits record high of 2650.3 at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian All Ordinaries hits record high of 2650.3 at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened at a new record high on Friday, the market buoyed by takeover speculation for food ingredients group Burns Philp & Co and after the Dow added 136 points on Thursday.
At 10.17 a.m. (0017 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 12.2 points firmer at a record high of 2,650.3, exceeding Thursday's intra-day record of 2,646.4.
The June share price index was 10 points up at 2,663 and at a 12.7 point premium to the underlying index.
Burns Philp shares jumped sharply after an unidentified purchaser bought 78.16 million shares before the start of trade.

Brokerage Deutsche Morgan Grenfell earlier confirmed it had bought the shares, equivalent to about 14.7 percent of the company's issues capital, for a client who was not an international food group at a price of A$2.50 per share (US$1.88).

"One significant leg of the transaction has already been completed with the 15 percent bought this morning. You would have to say there was now the distinct possibility of a takeover offer (for Burns Philp)," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer from Sydney firm, Shaw Stockbroking.
Burns Philp shares were 37 cents higher at A$2.40 after touching a 13 month high at A$2.51 at the start of trade.

Spiteri said investors took the opportunity to take profits on Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) stock after the bank's shares touched a record high of A$10.00 on Thursday on takeover speculation.
ANZ shares were 29.2 cents or about three percent weaker at A$9.49 on turnover of 794,748 shares.
Investors were seen switching into Westpac Banking Corp shares which were 19.7 cents firmer at A$7.56.
Turnover was relatively light. Dealers said some investors were disappointed the Reserve Bank did not move to cut rates after Thursday's weaker-than-expected employment data.
